title: Rosalind and the Spire
premise: Kestrel Crane, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead trapped in ivory and bone, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things—until the crown declares a hunt for the gifted and a dying guildmaster sells his name to save her own skin. Forced into the service of Inquisitor Vael, Kestrel discovers the king has been dead for years, his voice bound inside the Spire's crown by the regent-thing that wears him. To unbind the king, Kestrel must gather the three bones of the original binding, betrayed at every turn by allies who want the throne for themselves, including the guildmaster he trusted most. In the end Kestrel shatters the crown in the Spire's heart, freeing the dead king's voice at the cost of his own hearing—and chooses exile with the guild rather than a place in the new court, finally belonging among those who trade in impossible things.
about_author: Ulyana Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval guild ledgers before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about bureaucracy, grief, and the small magics hidden in paperwork.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Kestrel Crane balances the guild's accounts, carving a memory of a drowned girl into whalebone while her ghost dictates her last words. POV: Kestrel. Establishes his gift, the guild's rules, and his careful anonymity. Emotional beat: quiet contentment built on concealment—the calm before the hunt begins.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Ash
chapters.summary: Criers announce the king's edict: all gifted must register or be burned. The guildmaster, Odile Voss, burns half the ledger to hide names—including Kestrel's. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: fear curdling into betrayal as he realizes how expendable he is.

chapters.title: What the Dead King Says
chapters.summary: A fragment of royal seal-bone arrives for appraisal; through it Kestrel hears a king screaming that he is not dead, only bound. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: horrified fascination—the first hook of the larger mystery.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vael Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Vael raids the guildhall with a list of names; Odile trades Kestrel's services for the guild's survival. He is collared with a mute-band that dampens his gift. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness, dragged from hiding into the hunt itself.

chapters.title: The Collar and the Cage
chapters.summary: Marched to the capital, Kestrel catalogs the Inquisition's vault of confiscated bones, each one whispering. He meets fellow prisoner Sera Quill, a hedge-witch who can hear his thoughts even through the collar. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: isolation broken by an unexpected ally.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: Brought before the king, Kestrel hears nothing from the man on the throne—but the crown above his head screams. Vael watches him too closely. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into certainty that the throne is hollow.

chapters.title: Sera's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera reveals she was caught trying to steal a relic: the first bone of the binding, a fingerbone of the old queen. She proposes escape and alliance. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: wary trust between two people trained to survive alone.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath
chapters.summary: They break into the Inquisition's deep vault; Kestrel's collar cracks in the relic's presence, restoring fragments of his hearing. They flee with the fingerbone. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by guilt over those left behind.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Hunted through the capital's undercity, they discover Odile has been feeding Vael information for years—she sold the original binding's secret long ago. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: grief for a mentor revealed as architect of everything.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Bones
chapters.summary: A blind mapmaker who reads bone like parchment tells them the second bone lies in a drowned monastery, guarded by the ghosts of monks bound mid-prayer. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: awe and terror at the scale of the old magic.

chapters.title: Drowned Prayers
chapters.summary: In the flooded monastery, Kestrel negotiates with the bound monks' chorus, promising release in exchange for the sternum of Saint Aldric. Sera nearly drowns holding the door. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: compassion tested against necessity—he must choose which dead to free first.

chapters.title: Two Bones, One Lie
chapters.summary: Comparing relics, Kestrel realizes the third bone is not lost—it is the crown itself, worn openly on the king's head. The binding was never hidden; it was enthroned. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: despair at the impossibility of reaching it.

chapters.title: Vael's Offer
chapters.summary: Captured again, Kestrel learns Vael knows the truth and serves the regent-thing willingly, believing order is worth any price. He offers Kestrel freedom and status if he binds the last free voices too. POV: Vael. Emotional beat: seduction of power, and Kestrel's refusal.

chapters.title: The Guild Remembers
chapters.summary: Escaping with Sera's help and the aid of guild smugglers, Kestrel finds Odile dying, poisoned by Vael. With her last breath she gives him the guild's master key and asks forgiveness. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: complicated mourning—forgiveness given without absolution.

chapters.title: A Kingdom of Whisperers
chapters.summary: The gifted underground rallies to Kestrel: bone-hearers, dream-readers, ash-speakers, all hunted, all willing. They plan to enter the Spire during the coronation renewal rite. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: belonging found at last—in community forged by persecution.

chapters.title: The Rite of Renewal
chapters.summary: During the annual ceremony where the regent renews its disguise, the underground infiltrates the Spire disguised as ritual servants. Half are taken; the plan frays. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: sacrifice and mounting dread as the clock runs out.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing Him
chapters.summary: Alone in the throne room, Kestrel speaks with the regent-thing, which shows him visions of power offered honestly: it was once a person too, consumed by the crown it stole. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: horror tempered by recognition—the theme of corruption made flesh.

chapters.title: Sera Falls
chapters.summary: Vael captures Sera and threatens to bind her voice into the crown as reinforcement unless Kestrel surrenders the two bones. He does. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: despair and fury—everything gained, lost in a single choice made out of love.

chapters.title: The Chorus in the Crown
chapters.summary: Bound beside the Spire's heart, Kestrel reaches through his gift into the crown and finds the true king's voice still fighting after fifteen years. Together they turn the binding inward. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: hope kindled in the darkest place.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax: the king's voice, the freed monks, and every ghost Kestrel ever carved rise through the Spire. The crown splits; the regent-thing unravels screaming; Vael dies defending the order he chose. Kestrel's hearing burns away in the release. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: triumphant devastation.

chapters.title: The Empty Throne
chapters.summary: The true king, restored but mortal and changed, offers Kestrel honors and a seat at court. Kestrel declines—power is just another crown. Sera, freed, chooses to stay and help rebuild. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: bittersweet parting of the closest of friends.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Free
chapters.summary: Kestrel returns to the guildhall, deaf to the dead but keeper now of a new ledger: names of the freed, the fallen, and the gifted no longer hunted. He opens the doors to anyone who knocks. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: peace earned—belonging chosen, not granted.
